(mod question) What do you want to see here in this sub?

To be honest I would like to see fewer posts. I am interested in VR but not that much. This is a small-ish sub but it sure gets a lot of posts - this has the effect of getting me to read almost nothing due to the spam.

Some posts are great - the Google and Sundance ones featured right now are pretty interesting, while this one: "OptonautA VR Camera for iOS" I will literally never read unless someone pays me to do it. I haven't read any of the 2 I mentioned though because there is just too much content being posted and I don't have the time to read everything. I am close enough to unsubscribing because it's adding little value to my Voat experience.

So my suggestion to you as a frequent poster here is to, instead of posting everything that is interesting that you find (even if it's pretty interesting) you select better which news to bring to the sub. Maybe one per day or two days at most? I know this would help me to have time to read them and actually come in and discuss. And discussion for me is better than having a lot of new posts coming in. You would be doing me a favor too since this is a great way to keep up-to-date with VR news :)

Anyway this is all my opinion and you can agree or disagree with it but maybe the fact that you posted this here and as I was writing the answer you already posted another article would go to show you I'm right.

EDIT: actually the other way around, this post came second. The argument still stands though.

ah good feedback. Truth is, I'm not at all sure what folks are looking for. It's why I asked. Some are after dev resources, some (like me ) are all about the VR film world, some are unity/oculus folks... ect. etc... So trying to get content that various groups are after is always a challenge. but... good feedback, will keep it in mind!

So to better answer your question: I like "big picture" posts as a way to keep up-to-date with the VR industry. I work with technology so this sub is a great opportunity for that. I am not an specialist though so specific game or product reviews are not interesting to me unless they are groundbreaking or extremely interesting and thus are big news in the industry.

I'll use some examples about what are "big picture" posts to me:

  • Googles New Head of Virtual Reality on What Theyre Planning Next -> Google's new strategy for VR? You can't get much bigger than that!
  • Virtual Reality: the immersive film-making wowing Sundance -> Again, Sundance is a big name in the movies industry
  • Super Bowl 50 Will Have VR Headsets To Put Fans In The Game -> Again superbowl is a big name and it is interesting to see VR being adopted in a wide-spread manner and outside the context of video-games
  • Nvidia unveils two SDKs to power virtual reality graphics processing -> Again NVidia is a huge name, especially in the industry. I also like that this pretty factual and down to earth - it's discussing specific technology that is here already (or coming very soon)

Now I will get some top posts from the last week and tell you why they don't interest me at all:

  • I watched someone commit suicide in VR and it freaked me out -> any suicide is freaky, what does this have to do with VR?
  • You can watch 13 of the best VR films at Sundance from your home right now -> No I can't because I don't have time to watch 13 VR movies or the hardware to do it on
  • For VR to be truly immersive, it needs convincing sound to match -> Just like any non-VR video-game or movie. Almost looks like the article is using the VR buzzword to sell the entire article
  • How To Play PC Games With VR Google Cardboard as an Oculus -> I'll play PC games on my PC, Cardboard games on Cardboard and Oculus games on Oculus if and when I buy one of them
  • Oculus Story Studio University to Bring VR Film Workshops to NYU and USC -> Not interested in things that are going to happen possibly in the near future, more interested in facts, interviews, reviews and news about recent events. Also I'm not going to NYU or USC.

Alright, I hope this was more of the kind of feedback you were looking for even if it's all just personal opinion.
